newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WMC accelerates Olympic Dam expansion.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WMC accelerates Olympic Dam expansion.

text.p: WMC Ltd said on Wednesday its planned acceleration of the Olympic Dam mine project in South Australia was expected to cost A$1.48 billion including a A$120 million allowance for possible cost acceleration.

WMC said in July last year when it announced the Olympic Dam expansion that it planned to invest A$1.25 billion to more than double production at the copper/uranium/silver/gold mine in South Australia to about 200,000 tonnes per annum by 2001.
It also said then it saw copper production rising from its current 85,000 tonnes per annum to 150,000 tonnes by 1999.
WMC said in its results statement for the six months to December 31 that the acceleration of the project meant it now aimed to reach 200,000 tonnes of refined copper by the end of 1999.
"To achieve this acceleration of the expansion, the overall capital cost is expected to be A$1.48 billion including A$0.12 billion allowance for possible cost escalation," WMC said.

WMC managing director Hugh Morgan told a news conference that Olympic Dam's uranium output at the end of 1999 would be over 3,700 tonnes and gold production would be roughly 75,000 ounces, while silver production would hit one million ounces.
Earlier, WMC announced a 46.4 percent fall in its net profit to A$96.5 million, due largely to a slump in profit from the nickel division to A$64.4 million from A$151.9 million.
The lower nickel profit was due to a 16.7 percent fall in US$ cash nickel prices and a 6.4 percent higher Australian dollar.
